short: A major English victory that halted a Scottish invasion during the Anarchy.
full:
On 22 August 1138, an English army fought back a major Scottish invasion at Cowton Moor near Northallerton, Yorkshire. King David I of Scotland had invaded northern England ostensibly to support the claim of his niece, Empress Matilda, to the English throne, though also to expand his own territory. The English forces, rallied by Archbishop Thurstan of York, marched under a ship's mast bearing the consecrated banners of northern saints, giving the battle its name.

The English deployed a combination of dismounted knights and archers, whose continuous fire decimated the unarmoured Scottish infantry attempting to charge the lines. David's army was thoroughly defeated and forced to retreat. Despite the tactical victory, King Stephen later ceded substantial northern territories to the Scots to secure peace and focus his military efforts on the civil war in the south.
